cues:
The title ‘Samilshingo’ (三一神誥)
literally translates to

“to expound on
the ‘3 yet 1 God’”.
So it is saying,

“Let me tell you about
the 3 forms of God.”
Actually, if you go to the very source,

it makes more sense for this to be
Hwanung’s teachings, not Dangun’s.

We should be proud that there is such a scripture
from Korea that explains God so precisely.

The theological contents from Muslim scholars
who study the『Quran』are the same as Samilshingo.

The description of God from the『Upanishad』
is also the same as Samilshingo.
It's all the same.
How can it all be the same?

"The place which is
immeasurable, completely empty,

beyond time and space, unnamable,
that's where the universe sprang from."

This is the same explanation
that’s common across the world.

When Samilshingo says
it’ll expound on the ‘3 yet 1 God’,

the ‘God’ in this context
is referring to both a personal God,
and also the universal, impersonal God.

So when it says it’ll talk
about the 3 forms of God,

we can confidently foresee that it’ll be talking
about Mugeuk, Taegeuk, and Hwanggeuk.

Thus, in the Chapter 1 it mainly
talks about Mugeuk (無極),

in Chapter 2 it mainly
talks about Taegeuk (太極),

and in Chapter 3 it mainly
talks about Hwanggeuk (皇極).
You should be able to foresee this.

In other words, in Chapter 1 it talks about
the transcendent source of the universe,

in Chapter 2 it talks about the form of God
as He creates the universe,

and in Chapter 3 it talks about
how this God governs the universe.

The ‘God’ in the Samilshingo
can sometimes refer to

the complete, ego-transcendent God
who created the universe,

but also it can sometimes refer to the most
holy being among humans — the personal God.

Our ancestors used
both meanings of the word.

So when it says ‘God’,
it can refer to the God who

actually manages the universe
from the North Star,

and it can also refer to the source of the universe
which created Heaven, Earth, and Man.

Dangun says,
"My great follower Paengwu!

To you I shall expound on ‘Heaven’
(God as Existence, the Self of Mugeuk).”

Now, why do you think
I use the term ‘Self of Mugeuk’?
While you are listening to this right now,

you can't just think,
"Wow, I guess such a thing exists."
This is about you.

It’s talking about the ‘you’ within you
right now which is the Self of Mugeuk.
That is Heaven.

Now, what else did I call this Mugeuk?
“God as Existence”.
As for Taegeuk?

I called it ‘God as Creator’ since it is the
seed that creates Heaven, Earth, and Man.

And for Hwanggeuk?
‘God as Ruler’.

However, in this first chapter, it speaks of God
with more emphasis on God as Existence.

“The Heaven I am trying to
speak of is not that blue sky

nor is it that dark sky
you see with your eyes.

Such a sky is merely a sky
made up of energy,

so it is only a sky
in opposition to land.

The Heaven I am talking about
is the Heaven as the Source

which created that blue and black sky
and that land where you stand on.

This Heaven I speak of
hasn’t the slightest bit of form

nor the slightest bit of a fixed basis.
It has no beginning or end."
It’s saying it has no basis in time and space.

"It has no beginning or end, and it has
no distinction between up and down,

or north, east, south, and west.
It is merely completely empty,

and yet there isn’t a place it doesn’t exist
nor a thing it doesn’t embrace.

Only such a place is indeed
the place which is the Essence of God.”

“This first chapter explains
not the natural sky,

but Mugeuk: the basis of Taegeuk
which is the root of all things.”
So when it says ‘the basis of Taegeuk’,

it’s implied that Taegeuk
is already being presupposed here.

Therefore, it’s not talking about
Mugeuk as merely emptiness,

but rather says “The God which is
the root of all things, is originally empty.”

and speaks of Mugeuk
in relation to Taegeuk.

The sentences are simple
and it’s only a few words,

but contained within are some quite profound
theological and philosophical explanations.

This isn’t something that
someone can just write on a whim.

Now moving on to Chapter 2,
‘God’ is now referring to

the God as Creator,
or the Self of Taeguk.

“The Self of Taegeuk
exists at the very first place
where there is no more above.”

The place where there is
no more above is the apex.

It exists at the very apex
of your mind as well.

Stop conceptualizing this
as something outside yourselves.

It’s the apex of your
thoughts, emotions, and 5 senses.

If you try searching outwards,
you’ll find nothing other than

the objects of your
thoughts, emotions, and 5 senses.

Only when you go inwards
will you find the consciousness

that’s beyond your senses,
and if you go even further,

you’ll find the source
of that consciousness.

That dimension exists only within
your mind, not anywhere outside.

So you can only find something
more fundamental when you dive inwards.

Seek your mind, which is a
higher dimension than matter,

then seek the fundamental
essence of the mind.

And when you find that essence, know that
that’s the place which we call God.

Naturally we call it God
since mind and matter

all came from that place.
I hope you will understand it like this.
“God, the Self of Taegeuk,

exists at the very first place
where there is no more above.

With His great virtue,
great wisdom, and great strength,

God creates Heaven and
presides over countless worlds.”

Here, it has already extended
the meaning of God to

‘God as Ruler’,
or the ‘Self of Hwanggeuk’.

“He created every single thing in the universe,
and yet didn’t miss even the tiniest details.

Extremely bright and numinous,
with no way to dare name or calculate,

He presides
transcending all names and language.

However, if with sound and energy
you yearn and pray earnestly,

even this transcendent God
can be intimately seen.”

This part talks about
how to directly see God,

but since the explanation for the practice
and the principle of the practice

is very condensed in the original,
I’ve elaborated on it a bit.

“If you wish to directly see God yourself,
you must be able to entrust the entirety

of your discriminating
mind to God and rest.

When you transcend your ego
and become one with God,”

You have to transcend your ego
in order to become one with God.

When you are within your ego, you can
only stay at the periphery of the universe.

However, if you want to move
to the center of the universe,

you need to let go of your
thoughts, emotions, and 5 senses.
These have the property of periphery-ness.

When you let go of these things
within time and space,

then you will naturally go
outside time and space.

Right now, when we think,
laugh and cry, or feel our senses,

it makes us remain
within time and space.

But try letting go of all of the properties
of things within time and space.

Stop distinguishing between
subject and object, between I and others.
Forget about time and space.

If you just keep moving
in this direction of not knowing
with an attitude of ‘don’t know!’,

then instead of being an
existence within time and space,

you will be able to be the existence
at the center of the universe.
I encourage you to actually try this.

“Then you will realize that
you were originally never separated from God.

It is because only things of the same substance
can know each other completely.”

The fact that we are able to understand God
implies that there is a divine nature within us.

That divinity has been
within us since the beginning.

If it was never there,
then we wouldn’t even have to attempt to understand.
This means that God is already within us.

“God has already come down
and exists within your head.
How could you have seen and felt God

if He who presides over everything
didn’t exist as your essence?”

Let’s say you felt God
or something divine while meditating.

Understand that you were only able to feel it
because divinity already existed within you.
You just wouldn’t be able to detect it.
How would you,

who can’t even see colors
outside the visible spectrum,
be able to see God?

Because the ability to recognize God
is already within us.

And since only things of the same substance
can know each other,
it means there is divinity within us.
“Therefore, ultimately,

you must seek for the seed of God
within your innate nature.”

So instead of searching outwards,
search inwards.

“Your innate nature transcends
time and space and is completely empty,

and yet there isn’t a place it doesn’t exist
nor a thing it doesn’t embrace.”

“Within your empty innate nature already lies
the virtue, wisdom, and strength of God as a seed.
Therefore, you must search for that seed,

through which you can achieve
God-like virtue, wisdom, and strength,

nowhere else than from
within your own innate nature.

While resting within your innate nature
which is the seed of God,

you must govern your
thoughts, emotions, and 5 senses

by clearing away all the
impurities of the ego

which block your God-like virtue,
wisdom, and strength from actualizing.”

“While precisely perceiving the virtuous,
unitive, wise, and self-evident Truth as is,
you must fully cultivate that seed

which allows you to realize
that omnipotent Truth in reality.

When you regain and abide
within your innate nature,
purify the ego,

and fully cultivate the
virtue, wisdom, and strength of God,
you will become an avatar of God

and be qualified to
participate in God's cosmic work.”

You must participate in the
cosmic Great Humanitarianism work.

You must study with
this kind of goal in mind.
Now on to Chapter 3.
“That Heaven which surrounds us

is the Kingdom of God,
(God as Ruler, the Self of Hwanggeuk)”

It’s referring to the
divine nature within you.

When that God which governs
manifests as a human form,

we call that person
‘the God among humans’.

So the God among humans lives at the
apex of the sky called the North Star.

But before that, think about how amazing
it would’ve been for the ancient people.

Since they had nothing to do at night,
they probably stared at the stars in the night sky.

They found that all night long,
all the stars in the night sky rotate around a single axis.
And the star at that center axis didn’t move.

So since all the other stars
rotated around this center star,

they said, “That must be
the apex of the universe where God lives.”

But also, when they searched spiritually,
they realized that there was a place

which corresponded to the
North Star in the spiritual world.

In actuality, that spiritual world
is of more importance to us.

It’s just using an analogy
with the visible world.

So when it says the ‘North Star’,
don’t only just think of the North Star in the material world.

“That North Star of the spiritual world
is where the Palace of God exists.

This place can only be reached
by climbing all kinds of goodness as its staircase
and passing through all kinds of virtue as its gateway.
As the place where the one and only God abides

and where many philosophers
and divine people escort and receive Him,
it is greatly propitious and greatly luminous.”
“Just as there is a Palace of God within Heaven,

there is a Palace of God
within the microcosm of our body.”

So there is a North Star within our body
as well, located in our upper dantian.

“It is our skull. Therefore, only the person
who has clearly become

one with their innate nature
which is God who exists in our skull,

has fully acquired the virtue,
wisdom, and strength of God,

and has accomplished
all sorts of good deeds

can ascend up to the Palace of God to meet
God directly and enjoy eternal pleasure.”

So you can actually go to
the North Star, the Kingdom of God,

but only if you think, feel, and act
in accordance with God’s will,

or Seongtonggongwan (性通功完),
in this reality of ours.

“This third chapter explains
the ‘personal Hwanggeuk’

which governs a person,
and how to realize that Hwanggeuk.”

Lastly, I will discuss
the last part of Chapter 5

where it explains the actual details of
the practice method Samilshingo expounds.

“For sentient beings,
since good and evil,

clear and murky, and
thick and thin are all mixed together,

they follow as they please
whatever they encounter,”

Since these factors are
all complexly intertwined,
there are an infinite number of combinations

depending on the level of clarity,
or the level of thinness, etc.

“which makes them fall
into the painful sequence

of being born, growing,
aging, getting sick, and dying.”

“However, if the wise man practices
‘the cessation of feelings’ (止感),

‘breathing evenly’ (調息),
and ‘the restraint of touch’ (禁觸),

and transforms and disciplines
themselves with an unwavering mind,

they are able to revert
their delusions and become true.”
So, you are able to change the mind

or feeling within yourself that was
lurking towards evil into good,

change the energy which was
becoming murky to become clear,

and change the lifeforce that was
thinning out to become thick again.

Now it describes each of the
three practices in more detail.

First, let’s see what can be accomplished
through ‘the cessation of feelings’.
“If through ‘the cessation of feelings’,

one governs and transcends the totality
of their thoughts and emotions,”

You must be able to govern happiness
and anger to maintain its appropriateness,

but also be able to just
totally transcend them as well.

“and clearly becomes one
with their true innate nature of

love, justice, harmony, and wisdom
which transcends good and evil,

then they become able to
make their mind extremely good

and wholly realize the goodness of
love, justice, harmony, and wisdom

within the phenomenal world,
thus acquiring great ‘virtue’.”

Since one has precisely
understood their innate nature,

they are able to always keep their mind good,
not letting it steer towards evil,

and also able to fully realize
their innate nature of

love, justice, harmony, and wisdom
on this earth of ours.

“If through ‘breathing evenly’,
one governs the totality of their energy,”

When you are able to
breathe evenly well,

you become able to
control the energy in your body.

You can choose to completely
gather it within your dantian,

or also circulate it
throughout your entire body.

When so, you attain the precise wisdom
of how energy operates as well.

“If one realizes the true vital energy
which transcends clearness or murkiness,

then they can make their lifespan
the same as Heaven and Earth

and realize the harmonious functions
of the energy of yin yang wuxing

by freely governing energy
within the phenomenal world,
thus achieving great ‘wisdom’.”

Now, see how much importance
the practice of ‘the restraint of touch’ has.
“If through ‘the restraint of touch’,

one governs and transcends
the totality of their senses,

then they become able to preserve the true essence
which transcends thickness and thinness,
make their body precious and lustrous,

and freely perform good deeds
while eliminating evil

within the phenomenal world,
thus achieving great ‘strength’.”
If you restrain your senses,

doesn’t this mean you have acquired
the practical strength to realize goodness?
If you restrain your senses well,

you gain practical strength
within the phenomenal world.

Next, it explains what occurs
in each of the three dimensions
corresponding to our three dantians.

“In the dimension of thinking
(upper dantian 上丹田),

the sky-like well-rounded wisdom
in which both spiritual wisdom

and the wisdom of the phenomenal world
are evenly combined is achieved.”

“In the dimension of emotions
(middle dantian 中丹田),

the great virtue which doesn’t see others
as separate from oneself is achieved.”

“In the dimension of the 5 senses
(lower dantian 下丹田),

all kinds of goodness
and virtue are actualized at will,”

Now, remember that there are two sides
for the dimension of the 5 senses.

There is the energy body aspect
and the physical body aspect.

So, you are able to make the
energy body which grants eternal life,

but also in actuality, your ability
to act good becomes excellent

and you gain the strength to actualize
all kinds of goodness and virtue at will.
So speaking on the energy body aspect,

it says,“Achieve the body of eternal life
so that the infinite strength

to manifest that body
anywhere at will is achieved.”
The entire picture is contained here, isn’t it.
“As such, if through practicing these 3 methods,

one clearly realizes their true character
to become clearly one with their innate nature
and attains the eternal lifeforce, abundant essence,

and thoroughly attains the virtue, wisdom,
and strength to complete the ‘good deed’,”
When all of these are attained, what happens?

“You become a true avatar of God and will truly
participate in God’s all-encompassing work

of creating and sustaining all things
by participating in Heaven and Earth.
In the original text of Samilshingo,

it just emphasized the part about
going to Heaven and enjoying eternal pleasure,

but I added this commentary
so you don’t get the wrong impression.

I mean, what do you think you’d do
when you’re in the Kingdom of God?

It’s like saying if you keep working hard
as a government official at the state level,

you’ll eventually come to the White House
to enjoy eternal pleasure.
Then it seems like

the White House is where you go
to attain eternal pleasure, right?

But what would you actually
do instead once you get there?
You become a true participant in God’s work

since you’re now at the hub of the universe
where they spread

The Great Humanitarianism ideal
all across the universe.

Also, in the mythology in Samguk Yusa,
it says that God came down to earth

because he wanted to
benefit humanity far and wide.

Then what do you think
they’re researching up there,

in the White House of the universe,
the North Star?

It’s not a place where they’re just
only delighting in eternal pleasure.

Pleasure is a given since they’ve
freed themselves of all afflictions,

but what they actually conduct
is the cosmic Great Humanitarianism work.

And so, if it’s the time to level up earth,
they come down to earth and conduct their work.

In the mythology, it says 10,000 years ago
Hwanung came down from Heaven

with 3,000 of his followers
during the ancient era

and taught the people on how to live properly
in every corner of their lives.

How to eat, how to conduct marriages,
how to manage societies,

but moreover, to do so
with the Great Humanitarianism ideal.

He also taught them
the training method of

‘cessation of feelings’, ‘breathing evenly’,
‘restraint of touch’ and also on philosophy.

This is the true meaning of
‘to complete the deed’ (功完).
